subject: AcroPay integration: secure ingest, key ops, and embed routing — postcall recap
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@acropay.com>, Maya Singh <maya@acropay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: AcroPay integration: secure ingest, key ops, and embed routing — postcall recap

Hi Alex / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the integration track: 

1) Architecture & auth model (priority)
   - You prefer scoped service accounts for the ingestion pipeline (short-lived JWTs minted by AcroPay KMS) rather than long-lived API keys — agreed.
   - We recommended Redwood short-lived API tokens backed by your OIDC provider for customer-sent requests (embeddings/retokenization), and service-account JWTs for server-to-server ingestion.

2) SDK onboarding and sample artifacts
   - Attaching a small SDK bundle and a minimal code snippet for service-account JWT exchange + example structured-output tool-calling payloads.

3) Embed/rerank routing and costs
   - We'll propose a routing policy that directs high-recall requests to the larger embedding model (emb-large) and lower-latency queries to emb-compact. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quantization settings after 48–72 hours of telemetry.

4) Security evidence and next steps for procurement
   - You asked for SOC2 artifact list + a short note on retention of audit logs. Ben will follow up with the standard evidence pack and a proposed contract appendix for key rotation SLA.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- AcroPay: confirm which KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, or on-prem HSM) you will use for service-account signing — Alex/Maya by Tue 6/2 EOD.
- Redwood (Ben): send SOC2 evidence pack and a draft contract clause for key rotation and token TTLs — by Mon 6/1.
- Redwood (Aditya): prepare a short runbook (2–3 pages) describing the JWT exchange flow and a minimal SDK example picked for your stack (Go + Node) — by Wed 6/3.

Attachments: acropay-credentialing-checklist.pdf (checklist you can fill), redwood-sdk-snippet.tar.gz (sample code + README).

If anything above is off, please flag — otherwise we'll treat these as the agreed actions and track in the HubSpot deal.

Thanks,

Chloe Martin
Enterprise Lead, Integrations
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@acropay.com>

Cc: Maya Singh <maya@acropay.com>, security@acropay.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcroPay integration: secure ingest, key ops, and embed routing — postcall recap

Hi Chloe —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- KMS: we'll standardize on AWS KMS for the first phase; on-prem HSM is a later option but not for initial launch.
- JWTs: we asked about refresh cadence. Can you confirm recommended token TTLs for service-account JWTs vs Redwood short-lived API tokens?
- SOC2 pack: great — please make sure the pack includes our retention policy question answered (30/90/365 day retention options).

We'll aim to confirm KMS choice by Tue 6/2. I also looped in security@acropay.com to flag any compliance blockers early.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform Integrations
AcroPay
alex.dunne@acropay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: AcroPay SOC2 pack + contract note (draft)

Chloe / Aditya —

Per the call, I put together a minimal evidence pack and a draft clause that addresses: key rotation cadence, short-lived token TTLs, audit log retention, and emergency key compromise procedures. Attached to this thread: acropay-credentialing-checklist.pdf (filled where possible) and a .docx with proposed language. Highlights below: 

- Recommended rotation cadence: service-account signing keys rotated every 90 days; private signing material never stored in plaintext on Redwood; our runtime supports immediate revocation by invalidating session tokens.
- Token TTLs: suggested defaults — service-account JWTs (signed by customer KMS): 15m–1h; Redwood short-lived API tokens (for SDKs/clients): 15m with automatic refresh via OIDC exchange. We can parameterize these per-contract.
- Audit logs: default 90 days retention for standard plans; 365+ available as an add-on.

Aditya: can you confirm that our SDK snippets show a sample refresh flow (client -> OIDC -> mint token -> call Redwood)? If not, flag and I'll hold sending the doc.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@acropay.com>, Maya Singh <maya@acropay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcroPay integration: secure ingest, key ops, and embed routing — postcall recap

Alex / Maya —

Thanks for the fast reply and for looping security in. Quick responses to the two asks: 

- KMS: AWS KMS is totally fine for the initial phase — we'll annotate the runbook for AWS KMS specifics (key policies, signing permissions).
- Token TTLs: Ben's draft covers this; we default to short TTLs but can extend per contract. For clarity: service-account JWTs signed by AcroPay KMS should be minted with a 30m TTL for ingestion jobs that require batching; Redwood short-lived API tokens (for direct API calls or SDKs) we recommend 15m with automatic refresh. If you need 1h for large batch jobs, we can support that under a contractual exception.

Next steps: please confirm KMS by Tue 6/2 and we'll (Ben/Aditya) deliver the evidence pack + runbook by the dates in the recap. We'll open a HubSpot task and ping you when artifacts are uploaded.

Best,
Chloe
